newsitem.title: INDIA: India cabinet to take up divestment proposals.
newsitem.headline: India cabinet to take up divestment proposals.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Saturday Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's cabinet is likely to discuss the sale of shares in three state-owned units next week.

The Disinvestment Commission, set up by the ruling United Front government last year to advise on a partial privatisation programme, has recommended in three separate reports the sale of shares in 15 state-owned units.
"We went to cabinet and two weeks ago cabinet cleared the modalities of processing these recommendations," Chidambaram told a news conference.
"Once we have got cabinet approval for that, we have now gone back to cabinet with specific disinvestment proposals of three companies."
Chidambaram hoped that Gujral's cabinet would discuss the disinvestment proposals next week. "Once cabinet gives us the clearance we will proceed with the disinvestment in three companies."
He declined to name the three state-owned units.

The Indian government, in its budget for 1997/98 (April-March), proposed to raise 48 billion rupees from the sale of shares in state-owned firms during the year, compared with a target of 50 billion for 1996/97.
